subject.title: fix(browser): keep guarded CDP sockets on validated endpoints [AI]

question: Should strict Browser CDP policy deliberately make existing Chrome MCP profiles with an explicit remote `cdpUrl` unavailable until Chrome MCP can accept OpenClaw's validated DNS pin?
rationale: This is a security-versus-compatibility product boundary: retaining Chrome MCP attach would leave an unpinned transport path, while failing closed can stop existing restricted profiles at runtime.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Preserve the restriction, document the upgrade path, and require real proof that guarded OpenClaw-driver connections remain pinned.

options.title: Preserve Chrome MCP attach temporarily
options.body: Keep the current attach behavior until an upstream-compatible pinned transport or an explicit opt-in strict mode is available.

options.title: Narrow the supported policy combinations
options.body: Define and document a smaller set of restrictive CDP policies for which Chrome MCP remains supported without a pinned socket.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Preserve the restriction, document the upgrade path, and require real proof that guarded OpenClaw-driver connections remain pinned.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main Browser ownership could not be established from the available read-only evidence, so the decision should be routed through the Browser area review path rather than attributed to the PR author.
